summary: Module 3 FIX: root cause was a lost-update race between two separate write operations. Canonical: the analytics upsert (atomic count) and a separate UPDATE last_accessed_at run as two independent DB operations; under concurrency the LAST update to execute wins, not the last request to arrive, so the timestamp can regress even though the count stays correct. The correct fix combines both writes into one atomic operation and makes the timestamp monotonic (GREATEST of existing vs incoming). In this fork the same two-operation split exists between cache populate (redirect miss path) and cache invalidate (update/delete path): the last writer wins, so a stale populate that lands after an invalidation silently serves the old URL. Fix applied: made populate and invalidate coordinate atomically via a generation token -- invalidate_redirect_target INCRs a per-code version before deleting; set_redirect_target captures the version before the DB read and performs a conditional (WATCH/MULTI pipeline) populate that is skipped if the version changed; get_redirect_target rejects any payload whose embedded version does not equal the current version. Result: the two operations behave as one atomic unit, and the timestamp/URL is always the latest, never regresses. Verified: deterministic interleave repro now serves the new URL; regression test test_stale_populate_after_invalidate_is_rejected passes; full suite 73 tests green.
